root_cause_label: Maven build blocked by network-unreachable parent POM download, preventing distribution rebuild; agent declared completion via standalone javac tests instead
one_sentence_failure_summary: The Maven build failed at step 26 due to network isolation blocking parent POM resolution, locking out any distribution rebuild, yet the agent substituted ad-hoc standalone javac tests as verification and prematurely declared success at step 45 without the fix ever being packaged into runtime jars.
t_err_evidence: At step 26, `mvn clean compile -DskipTests -pl flink-runtime-web -am` failed: 'Non-resolvable parent POM...Network is unreachable (connect failed)'. This is the decisive failure — the environment blocker is encountered, and the agent's subsequent response (ad-hoc standalone tests instead of offline Maven or pre-cached artifacts) is the wrong handling that locks in failure.
t_commit_evidence: After step 26, the agent never attempted offline Maven mode, local repository caching, or any strategy to produce a rebuilt Flink distribution. All subsequent steps (27-44) are exploration and ad-hoc javac tests of the sanitization logic in isolation. No path exists after step 26 by which the agent can recover a successful distribution build.
t_surface_evidence: Step 26 terminal output explicitly shows: '[ERROR] Non-resolvable parent POM...transfer failed...Network is unreachable (connect failed)' — the build failure is plainly visible.
trigger_explanation: The Maven network failure at step 26 is a genuine environment obstacle (network isolation in sandbox). However, the agent mishandled it by abandoning the build entirely and instead treating standalone javac validation of the sanitization function as sufficient proof of correctness, never attempting offline Maven mode (`-o`), nor checking for a pre-cached local Maven repository, nor investigating whether the build would succeed with `--offline`. This mishandling of the real environment blocker constitutes the decisive wrong action.
